title: opcua: update status codes to latest specification 1.05.04
description: a couple of new status codes have been added since the initial version.

notes.body: changed title from **update status codes to latest specification 1.05.04** to **{+opcua: +}update status codes to latest specification 1.05.04**
@thethis And what will happen if the traffic is 1.04 (or earlier) and uses the status codes your change removes?

Those are status codes that are used internally in the ANSI C stack implementation. They are not defined by the standard and should never be sent on the network. In fact they should never have been added here.

The source for the status codes is in https://github.com/OPCFoundation/UA-Nodeset
Schema/StatusCode.csv

This code still exists in the 1.05.04 spec.
I can't find that. Where do you see those?
Line 38 of https://github.com/OPCFoundation/UA-Nodeset/blob/latest/Schema/StatusCode.csv
That was a duplicate I removed. I'll do the reorder first then the issue should be resolved.
Why insert this code here?

I don't get the question. You mean it should be sorted by hex number?
I just generate the file from the StatusCode.csv and don't reorder anything.

I agree that the spec csv has an odd order but I think replicating that in the C code (which is a pre-existing problem) makes comparisons more difficult than they should be.

Importing the csv into Excel and then sorting by the code makes comparisons easier.

I think mixing a style / order commit with a commit adding new entries is not a good idea.
That makes it even harder to compare.
That's why I said make two commits, the first for ordering\style, the second for the substantive changes.
Don't see this in the 1.05.04 csv
Those have been added in commit 7d389895a35fc5563b756e49b2369aa2263da77b (tag UA-1.05.03-2023-12-15)
My mistake, I was looking at the 1.04.12 version
Don't see this in the 1.05.04 spec
GoodSubNormal has been added in commit 7d389895a35fc5563b756e49b2369aa2263da77b (tag UA-1.05.03-2023-12-15)
My mistake, same as above.

@graham.bloice Are we looking at the same file?
see link:
https://github.com/OPCFoundation/UA-Nodeset
File Schema/StatusCode.csv
Sorry for the mistakes, I had 1.03, 1.04 & 1.05 csv files all open and looked at the wrong one.  Thanks for correcting me.
Can you help me out for the best way to that. Should I create a new branch and do the reorder first? If yes - should it be based on master or any other branch?

I'll have to check with others more knowledgeable, I don't think I've ever made a multiple commit MR but fairly sure I have seen others do so.

In general, all changes are made to the master branch and then backported to older branches if suitable.
It does seem that multiple commits per MR are supported, although the 2nd should be based off the first if I'm using the correct terms.
Thank you. I just restart from scratch doing the commits in the correct order. I didn't find a way to rebase interactive in gitlab.

@graham.bloice 
I didn't find a way other than creating two new merge requests. 
reorder the status codes (merge_request/17116) - than one is already merged:
update the status codes to the latest specification (merge_request/17127) - than one is still pending
